research_findings.headline: Creator reputation predicts a launch's CEILING, not whether it lifts off: repeat-graduator ANSEM rocketed 59x ($3.08M->$182.1M in 7d) while first-timer hehe matched it pump-for-pump (78x, $11.3K->$889K) but topped out ~200x smaller in absolute dollars -- refines repeat_deployer_reputation from a boolean into a graded creator-peak-mcap ceiling signal. Also: REQ-027 got its first-ever tight-span (<3600s) sample (WOJAK, span=1s, -0.77% loss), now N=11/15.

new_hypothesis.name: creator_prior_peak_mcap_ceiling_signal
new_hypothesis.mechanism: A creator's single BEST prior launch market cap (not just a boolean 'has graduated before') is a proxy for the size of the audience/KOL/MM network that creator can pull into a new launch. That network determines how HIGH a new token's mcap ceiling can go, independent of whether the token pumps at all in the first place (that's driven by generic launch mechanics -- narrative, timing, bundle structure -- which a cold first-time creator can also catch).
new_hypothesis.persistence: This is a graded, continuous signal (creator's historical peak mcap, bucketed into tiers) rather than a simple binary flag. The bot's existing repeat_deployer_reputation queue only captures 'has this creator graduated before' -- it does not weight by how big that prior graduation was. Distinguishing 'will it pump' (noisy, reputation doesn't help -- both ANSEM and hehe pumped comparably in %) from 'how big can it get if it pumps' (reputation-weighted, ANSEM's absolute ceiling was ~200x hehe's) is a distinction no current tool or prior research run has made -- it survives because most creator-reputation checks stop at boolean has-graduated-before.
new_hypothesis.entry_rules: Phase-1 LOG-ONLY, piggybacks on the already-queued repeat_deployer_reputation logger (do not build a separate one). When building that logger, capture the creator's HISTORICAL PEAK prior-launch mcap (not just a graduation count), bucket new launches by prior-peak tier (cold/no-history, nano <$100k, mid $100k-1M, mega >$1M), and log forward mcap trajectory (1h/24h/7d) per tier. No live filter change -- this only matters once the bucket-vs-ceiling relationship is confirmed at N>=20 per tier.
new_hypothesis.data_required: Same data source already scoped for repeat_deployer_reputation: pump.fun creator history (frontend-api-v3, free, no key) -- just capture one more field (prior launches' peak mcap, not only count). Zero new API surface.
new_hypothesis.evidence: N=2 exploratory, both from this run's watchlist follow-up (concrete mints + timestamps): ANSEM (9cRCn9rGT8V2imeM2BaKs13yhMEais3ruM3rPvTGpump), creator yHCxHBEaJW5tbndqC8JciSThr7U1cqLpdcsvHcx6PRe with prior peaks NORMIE $9.4M / TATE $604k / COBRA $362k / vibeshift $533k ('mega' tier) -- went $3.08M (07-12) -> $182.1M (07-19), +5,814%/59x. hehe (BreuhVohXX5fv6q41uyb3sojtAuGoGaiAhKBMtcrpump), first-time creator ('cold' tier, no prior graduation) -- went $11,280 (07-12) -> $888,688 (07-19), +7,776%/78x. Comparable % move, but ANSEM's absolute ceiling is ~205x hehe's. N=2 is anecdotal -- do not act until the logger accumulates a real per-tier sample.

subagents_dispatched.role: Novel mechanism hunt: bundler wallet reuse
subagents_dispatched.finding: Verdict: serial-bundler wallet-identity fingerprinting is ALREADY commoditized (Bubblemaps, GMGN, Trench Bot all expose cross-launch wallet-cluster reuse as a named signal) -- not a fresh edge, shelved. Found one genuinely unexplored alternative instead: post-bundle priority-fee-auction intensity (rising/dispersed CU-price curve in the 60-90s after a bundled launch = real organic competitive demand vs a bundler padding volume with more of its own flat-fee wallets). No tool productizes this. However, ZERO concrete evidence or backtested examples found this run -- flagged as a next-run research target, not promoted to this run's flagship hypothesis, since it lacks the evidence citation this brain's rules require.

ANSEM 59x'd to $182.1M (from $3.08M), hehe 78x'd to $888,688 (from $11,280) -- both pumped comparably in % terms but ANSEM's absolute ceiling is ~205x larger, feeding this run's new_hypothesis. Pump.fun's frontend-api-v3 sort/filter proved unreliable for isolating true last-24-48h graduations (returned stale May-2025-dated results regardless of sort param) -- could not produce the requested 3-5 fresh repeat-graduator examples within budget. Did surface one older (6-month-old prior grads) but clean repeat-graduator case: creator wc26h2qZphG7c7VBR8Mrz98LGZjsaaV44YZHBgaMpSa running a 'countries' token series (SPAIN, ARGENTINA, USA, Turkiye, Portugal, Norway, Netherlands, Germany, England, Croatia -- all graduated), useful as persistence evidence but not a fresh actionable watchlist entry.
